content.title: Davey Bosire Mogoko Oturi
content.summary: "I want to learn so I can teach others"

content.text: Davey Bosire got into nursing by mistake. The young man thought he was enrolled in a medicine course but by the time he realized his error - three months in - he had already fallen in love with being a nurse.

It's been 40 years since that fateful day and Davey still thinks nursing is a blessed profession. "We help people who can't help themselves, we speak for those who can't speak for themselves," he explains, "I love it."
"The biggest joy," he says, "is working with mothers because you can swiftly help them go from the severe pain of delivery to unspeakable happiness of holding their healthy child in their arms."

Davey also loves studying. He managed to get four diplomas as he worked full-time but could not afford his dream of getting a Bachelors' degree, as he had to support three children and four grandchildren. Davey had just gotten a comfortable job for the county government and was about to retire when he felt called to do more - particularly for mothers who, in his county, often receive very poor care.
After learning about the Bachelors' of Science in Midwifery at Aga Khan University, he applied and received the SONAM scholarship. Now he's feeling as ambitious as ever.

Davey admits that, at 62, he's got many medical advances to catch up on, but he is keen to learn. So far, he loves the Bachelor courses and says the members of staff have been really kind to him, especially those working in the IT department, who always take the time to walk him through computer tasks.

Not everyone was thrilled by Davey's academic choices. "Some people speak badly and say that I am too old to study," he says "but I only want to learn so that I can teach others." His family, however, is in full support of his Bachelors' ambition. His children get excited about his grades and even jokingly remind him to do his homework.

Davey says he encourages young Kenyans to consider a career in midwifery because it is easy to find employment, you can travel with your degree and, more importantly, it brings you happiness. "A woman comes in crying and soon after, you are smiling together," he says, "It's beautiful."

Retirement is no longer in the picture for Davey. After he graduates, his goal is to start his own private clinic back in his community to provide mothers and children with the quality care he's long seen missing in public facilities, which often lack in both training and equipment.

Davey hopes the clinic will create a positive ripple effect in his hometown, not just by improving patient outcomes but also by generating revenue for local shopkeepers and jobs for unemployed youths. His motto: "Just because you're getting old doesn't mean you have to be idle!"
